scope.description: Three-release deepening tranche for the 2000 Japan Rail stamp-rally prize rows: JR West Meowth row 196, JR East silver-course Mewtwo row 197, and JR East gold-course Eevee row 198. The tranche emphasizes rail-network participation, course-specific prize identity, English Wizards Black Star prints released in Japan, non-holo route variants, and traps against CoroCoro/Game Boy/League/Fan Club/Legendary Collection memories.

claims.text: The local source slice models one JR West Pokemon Stamp Rally 2000 prize row: Meowth row 196.

Bulbapedia says a non-holo version of the English Meowth print was released in Japan as a promotional card and awarded to passengers for completing the JR West Pokemon Stamp Rally 2000, held on Saturdays, Sundays, and public holidays between July 20 and August 27, 2000.
Bulbapedia identifies Meowth Wizards Promo 10 as illustrated by Kagemaru Himeno.
Bulbapedia distinguishes the JR West Japanese promotional copy as a non-holo version of the English print, separate from the earlier Japanese CoroCoro print and the Game Boy Color / Wizards paths.
This row matters because rail participation becomes provenance: a familiar English Meowth print entered the Japanese promo catalog through JR West stamp-rally completion.

narrative.human_title: JR West Stamp Rally 2000 — Meowth rides the rail network
narrative.why_it_matters: This is a perfect assembly object. Meowth was already a Game Boy and Wizards memory, but the JR West prize turns the same familiar cat into proof of movement through a railway event. A passenger had to participate in the stamp rally; the prize was not born from a booster pack or ordinary league kit. That makes the route the identity. A good agent should see the English card number, the non-holo Japanese release, the Kagemaru Himeno art, and the JR West map all at once.

Bulbapedia credits the English Wizards Promo 11 Eevee print to Kagemaru Himeno, while the separate Japanese Fan Club print uses Toshinao Aoki art.

narrative.human_title: JR East gold course — Eevee with a course boundary
narrative.why_it_matters: Eevee is dangerous in the best way for a catalogue: beloved, repeated, reprinted, and route-rich. This row is not just Eevee. It is the gold-course rail prize, a non-holo English Wizards print released in Japan after Fan Club and League paths had already given the same character other bodies. The agent has to feel the character pull, then refuse to let it erase the course boundary.
